title: Prelaunch security review and exception guidance
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, operational checklist and guidance for releases that touch RBAC v2, audit logging schema changes, SIEM export pipelines, or that require exception approvals. It is written for engineers shipping infra or platform changes and for security reviewers who must sign off pre-launch.

Scope:
- Any release that adds or modifies roles/permissions, changes audit log fields or formats, adds/changes SIEM export transforms, or introduces temporary exceptions to controls.
- Also used as the working template for evidence automation (what to collect automatically) and the exception approval form.

Quick summary checklist (high level, for release engineers):
- [ ] Create a changelog entry listing RBAC roles added/modified/deleted. Link to PRs.
- [ ] Run the RBAC role-sim tool against a representative org to validate least-privilege impact.
- [ ] Produce a sample of post-change audit events (sanitized) covering success/failure paths.
- [ ] Validate SIEM export pipeline mapping (field names/types) against SIEM ingestion tests.
- [ ] Add evidence artifacts to the release ticket and kick off evidence-collector automation.
- [ ] If any control cannot be met, submit an "exception request" with compensating controls and proposed expiry.
- [ ] Obtain security sign-off from at least two reviewers (one infra-focused, one product/security).

RBAC v2 specific checks (detailed):
- Role definitions and intent:
  - Confirm each new role has a one-line intent statement in the PR and the role catalog.
  - Map each role to minimum required APIs and specific model access (if applicable).
- Role composition and inheritance:
  - Verify inheritance graph has no cycles.
  - Ensure admin-level roles are split: org-admin vs infra-admin vs billing-admin.
- Permission granularity and resource scoping:
  - Ensure resource scoping is used where possible (project/org/model). No wildcard model access without explicit justification.
- Temporal/ephemeral privileges:
  - For temporary escalation, require timeboxed sessions with automatic revocation and audit flags.
- RBAC rule change testing:
  - Unit tests for permission checks.
  - Integration tests exercising grant/revoke and error paths (403/401).
  - Role-sim output attached to PR (summary + top-5 impacted principals).
- Migration / rollout guidance:
  - If migrating from RBAC v1 constructs, include a migration plan and rollback steps.
  - Rollout staged by org cohorts with monitoring for elevated error rates.

Audit log schema checklist and expectations:
- Backwards compatibility:
  - New fields should be additive where possible; deprecated field mappings must be documented.
- Required core fields (must exist in every event):
  - timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, result, request_id, region, service, host
- RBAC-linked fields to include when permission checks occur:
  - policy_version, granted_roles (list), effective_permissions (list, short), auth_method (token/kms/assumed-role)
- Data types and canonical formats:
  - timestamps in RFC3339, ids as UUIDs where available, booleans explicit.
- Example event (sanitized):
  - 2025-03-01T12:02:34Z | evt_01F... | actor_id:user-123 | action:grant-access | resource_type:model | resource_id:model-abc | result:success | policy_version:v2.1
- Sensitive data handling:
  - Never log raw request bodies containing PII or model outputs that include user-provided secrets. Use redaction tags and hash artifacts if needed.

SIEM export and parsing guidance:
- Export contract:
  - Define the export JSON schema version (e.g., audit_export_v3). Maintain a compatibility table in Confluence.
- Top-level mapping required by SIEM ingestion:
  - host -> host.name, service -> service.name, timestamp -> @timestamp, actor_id -> user.id, resource_id -> object.id, action -> event.action, result -> event.outcome
- Parsing rules to provide to SOC/Threat Detection teams:
  - Suggested Splunk/macros and Datadog processors with sample patterns. Attach sample search queries for common investigations (failed grants, token abuse).
- Throughput and backpressure considerations:
  - If schema adds large arrays (e.g., effective_permissions), consider compressing or summarizing for SIEM exports and rely on raw internal audit store for deep dives.
- Retention and legal hold:
  - SIEM ingestion TTL should be set per data-class. Audit exports intended for 90-day SOC use; extended retention must be justified and routed to secure object storage with access controls.

Evidence automation (what to collect, how):
- Minimum artifact set (automated via evidence-collector):
  - RBAC role catalog snapshot (JSON)
  - Role-sim report (PDF or JSON summary)
  - Sample audit events (10 success + 10 failure) with request_ids
  - SIEM test ingestion logs showing mapping success (ingest-recipient ack)
  - Unit and integration test run IDs and links to CI logs
  - Schema diff file (old vs new) and migration SQL/scripts if applicable
- Where to store artifacts:
  - Upload to release ticket attachments in Jira and to s3://redwood-evidence/releases/<release-id>/ (encrypted, lifecycle policy set).
- Automation triggers and ownership:
  - evidence-collector runs as part of pipeline job "collect-evidence" after merge to main for release branches. Security reviewer can invoke manual re-collection.
- Evidence TTL and auditability:
  - Artifacts kept for 1 year by default; critical production-impacting changes kept for 3 years. Each artifact must include a hash and artifact_id recorded in the release ticket.

Exception approval workflow (temporary deviations from controls):
- When to request an exception:
  - If a required control (e.g., strict resource scoping) cannot be satisfied before launch without causing customer impact.
- Exception request content (minimal required fields):
  - exception_id, requester, affected_control, reason, proposed_mitigation, expiry_timestamp, compensating_controls, risk_rating (low/med/high), rollout_scope, rollback_plan, evidentiary_artifacts (links)
- Reviewers and SLAs:
  - Default reviewers: Security Engineer (S), Product Owner (P), Infra Lead (I). For high-risk exceptions, also require SOC Lead.
  - SLA: 48 hours for regular, 72 hours for high-risk. If reviewers miss SLA, escalate to Head of Security.
- Approval conditions and controls:
  - Exceptions must include at least one compensating control (e.g., increased monitoring, shorter expiry, read-only access).
  - All approved exceptions must be recorded in the exceptions registry (Confluence table + alerting).
- Expiry and automatic remediation:
  - Exceptions should auto-expire. Where possible, automation must revoke the exception and notify owners. Manual re-review required for extensions.

Risk assessment quick matrix (for reviewers):
- Low: read-only visibility changes, non-prod environments, short-lived (<24h) dev testings.
- Medium: limited write permissions, production-facing but scoped to small customer subset, expiry <= 7 days, compensating monitoring in place.
- High: broad write permissions, cross-tenant access, model access to sensitive datasets, expiry > 7 days or no compensating control.

Sign-off template (to paste into Jira release ticket):
- Security sign-off:
  - Reviewer: <name>
  - Role: <security/infra/product>
  - Checklist items verified: RBAC_changes / Audit_events_sampled / SIEM_ingest_test / Evidence_present
  - Exceptions: none | exception_id(s)
  - Notes: <freeform>
  - Signed at: <YYYY-MM-DD>

Operational notes and gotchas (less formal):
- If RBAC change affects many tenants, expect a spike in 403 errors; add rapid-alerting and consider a canary rollout.
- When adding arrays to events (e.g., effective_permissions), SIEM dashboards may break if fields are not normalized — coordinate with SOC ahead of release.
- Don’t rely on SIEM for exhaustive forensic evidence; ensure raw audit store retention/immutability is sufficient for legal needs.
- For role-sim, sample orgs should include a cross-section: 1 small, 5 medium, 2 large (by number of principals and number of models).

Open questions / follow-ups (to resolve before final sign-off):
- Do we have a stable export versioning header in the audit pipeline that SOC can assert in its parsers? (RFC in Confluence linked above)
- Is there an automated remediation runbook for revoking temporary escalations if a scheduled job fails? (PR open: OPS-893)
- Confirm retention policy alignment with legal for model-related audit events (ticket LEG-1122).

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Run role-sim locally: ./tools/role-sim --org org-sample --roles pr-1234 --output role-sim-summary.json
- Collect evidence (CI job): .github/workflows/collect-evidence.yml -> job: collect-evidence -> artifact s3 path printed in job log
- Example Splunk query for failed grants:
  - index=audit sourcetype=redwood_audit action=grant-access result=failure | stats count by actor_id, resource_id, _time

Last edited by: Priya Nambiar (security)
Notes: this is intentionally concise; attach long-form migration plans or SIEM parsing playbooks as linked artifacts rather than embedding huge JSONs here.
